summary.text: Son of Anaxagoras in the native third of Argos — the royal line descended from Megapenthes that outlasted the Melampid and Biantid shares after the kingdom was divided in three.
Not to be confused with Alector son of Magnes in Thessaly, nor with the unrelated Alector names in the genealogies of Arcadia and Elis.

story.text: When Melampus cured the maddened women in the reign of Anaxagoras, son of Argeus, son of Megapenthes, Argos was split into three equal kingdoms. Anaxagoras kept the native third; Melampus and Bias received the other shares. Pausanias says the house of Anaxagoras ruled longer than the other two, and names Alector as his son in the succession that would pass through Iphis to Sthenelus son of Capaneus.
